name: keypulse
tagline: Find out which AI API keys are dead before your app does
short: Checks every AI provider key you have and tells dead keys apart from rate limits, retired models, and provider outages. Four causes, four different fixes.
medium: Free-tier AI keys die quietly — rotated, revoked, rate-limited, or the model gets dropped. Nothing tells you; your fallback chain just starts burning retries on a provider that will never answer. keypulse sends a real 1-token completion to each provider and reports exactly which failure it is.
long: Free-tier AI keys die quietly. They get rotated, revoked, rate-limited, or the model behind them is dropped from the free tier, and nothing surfaces it. Two of ours were dead for three weeks before anyone noticed. keypulse sends a real one-token completion to every configured provider, because listing models often succeeds with a key that cannot actually infer. It distinguishes DEAD_KEY (rotate it) from RATE_LIMIT (demote it, do not replace it) from NO_MODEL (change the model, not the key) from PROVIDER_DOWN (their problem) from BAD_RESPONSE, a 2xx with no usable completion, which is the dangerous case because callers treat it as success. Ships with ten providers verified live against real endpoints, and a --verify mode that re-checks every URL using a deliberately invalid key so the list can never rot unnoticed. Your keys are never printed or logged; only the environment variable name appears in output. Stdlib only, no dependencies, exit codes for cron and CI.
